title: LLVMhammer turns a DRAM bit flip into persistent LLM inference slowdown
dek: A Rowhammer-induced compiler fault yields correct but slower cached Triton GPU kernels across vendors.
evidence: Primary academic preprint; experimental threat model requires exploitable CPU DRAM faults
takeaway: Include compiled-kernel integrity and performance anomalies in inference supply-chain threat models.

sections.title: Context

bullets.lead: GPU kernels are compiled on CPUs
bullets.detail: Triton's JIT pipeline transforms GPU kernels through CPU-side MLIR/LLVM passes, then caches generated binaries for reuse.

paragraphs: GPU kernels are compiled on CPUs: Triton's JIT pipeline transforms GPU kernels through CPU-side MLIR/LLVM passes, then caches generated binaries for reuse.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Researchers show a Rowhammer-induced DRAM bit flip in a compiler optimization pass can yield a functionally correct but slower GPU kernel.
The suboptimal kernel is cached on disk, so later inference requests can remain slower after the transient memory fault has passed.

paragraphs: LLVMhammer attack: Researchers show a Rowhammer-induced DRAM bit flip in a compiler optimization pass can yield a functionally correct but slower GPU kernel.
Persistent effect: The suboptimal kernel is cached on disk, so later inference requests can remain slower after the transient memory fault has passed.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: The paper reports 4–16% increased single-GPU server latency across four LLMs on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX, and tests more severe output corruption.
The attack assumes an exploitable DRAM fault in the compilation environment, not a generic remote prompt injection or ordinary model failure.

paragraphs: Measured slowdown: The paper reports 4–16% increased single-GPU server latency across four LLMs on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX, and tests more severe output corruption.
Threat-model boundary: The attack assumes an exploitable DRAM fault in the compilation environment, not a generic remote prompt injection or ordinary model failure.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Protect JIT-generated artifacts and kernel caches, and monitor surprising performance shifts following recompilation.
Compare kernel hashes, output checks and latency baselines after system updates or suspected hardware faults.

paragraphs: Compilation belongs in supply-chain security: Protect JIT-generated artifacts and kernel caches, and monitor surprising performance shifts following recompilation.
Guard both speed and correctness: Compare kernel hashes, output checks and latency baselines after system updates or suspected hardware faults.
